item.title: Preview: RBNZ set to lift OCR to 3% ahead of election as oil and weak kiwi fuel inflation
item.description:
With a hike close to fully priced, the New Zealand dollar’s reaction is likely to hinge on guidance rather than the move itself, and the risk is asymmetric: a hold would catch markets badly offside and could trigger a sharp kiwi selloff. A hike paired with a clear tightening bias would be the most supportive outcome for the NZD and would push front-end yields higher, while “wait and see” language could see some of the priced peak trimmed. Oil remains the key external driver: further gains in crude linked to the Middle East conflict would feed straight into New Zealand’s fuel-heavy inflation outlook and strengthen the case for more hikes into 2027. AUD/NZD traders also face back-to-back central bank risk, with the RBA expected to hike again on November 3.

---

A pause looked likely in September, but rising fuel costs and a sliding kiwi have turned Wednesday’s RBNZ meeting into a near-certain pre-election hike.

Summary:

  • Economists and markets expect the RBNZ to raise the OCR by 25bp to 3% on Wednesday, its third straight hike after moves in July and September
  • Expectations for a pause after September have reversed as oil prices surged, the New Zealand dollar weakened and inflation pressures proved sticky
  • Annual CPI eased to 3.7% in the September quarter, below the RBNZ’s 3.9% forecast, but some economists see the December quarter above 4.5%
  • Markets price roughly a 90% chance of a hike and a peak near 3.5% by February; Westpac sees the OCR possibly reaching 4% by September 2027
  • ASB warns that a hold would likely sink the kiwi, with guidance on further tightening seen as the key market driver
  • The decision is due at 01:00 GMT Wednesday (21:00 ET Tuesday), ahead of New Zealand’s November 7 general election

The Reserve Bank of New Zealand is widely expected to raise its Official Cash Rate by 25 basis points to 3% on Wednesday, delivering a third consecutive hike as rising fuel costs and a weak currency threaten to push inflation further above its target band.

The call marks a turnaround from just weeks ago. After the RBNZ lifted the OCR to 2.75% in early September, Governor Anna Breman hinted at a pause, and bank economists were divided on whether October would bring another move. That debate has largely closed. According to interest.co.nz, economists at the country’s major banks now see a hike as almost certain, pointing to the surge in oil prices, further weakness in the New Zealand dollar and persistently sticky price pressures.

A Bloomberg survey also found that a majority of economists expect the OCR to rise to 3% this week. Inflation slowed in the third quarter, with annual CPI easing to 3.7% from 4.1% in June and coming in below the RBNZ’s 3.9% forecast. Many analysts expect it to accelerate again in the fourth quarter, however, with some projecting a December quarter reading of around 4.7%, which would leave inflation outside the 1% to 3% target band for longer than the central bank had projected.

Markets are positioned accordingly. ASB economists said pricing implies roughly a 90% probability of a 25 basis point increase, with a peak cash rate of around 3.5% expected by February. Westpac sees the tightening cycle running further, with the OCR possibly reaching 4% by September 2027. ASB has also warned that the prospect of hikes has been supporting the New Zealand dollar, and that a decision to hold would likely send the currency lower.

The timing adds a political dimension. The meeting falls just 10 days before the November 7 general election, although economists broadly expect the committee to set policy on economic grounds alone. Some argue the bank should go beyond a single move and signal that more tightening is coming, while others expect a short statement that leaves options open.

The decision is due at 01:00 GMT on Wednesday (21:00 ET on Tuesday). With a hike largely priced, the tone of the accompanying statement is likely to determine the market reaction. 

This article was written by Eamonn Sheridan at investinglive.com.

item.title: Bitcoin buyers are fighting back, but sellers aren't finished. Here are the two prices swing traders should watch
item.description:
Bitcoin tradeCompass update: Bearish scenario activated, first profit target reached

Bitcoin has moved below our $79,870 bearish threshold, with the latest supplied price near $79,438. The bullish threshold at $80,860 was briefly crossed but never sustainably confirmed.

The bearish scenario is now active, and TP1 at $79,630 has already been reached.

Here's what that means for traders following the tradeCompass plan:

  • Initial stop: The opposite bullish threshold at $80,860 served as the default stop reference for this short setup, subject to the trader's chosen execution and risk plan.

  • After TP1: A trader who entered near $79,870 and took an initial partial profit, for example 25% of the position, should now have moved the protective stop on the remaining 75% to the actual entry price, approximately $79,870.

  • Three remaining bearish targets: TP2 at $79,310, TP3 at $77,560 and TP4 at $73,680. These are potential objectives, not promises that Bitcoin will reach any or all of them.

What if Bitcoin reverses?

If Bitcoin rises and the remaining stop executes at the entry price, the trader retains the profit already taken at TP1, while the remaining position closes approximately at breakeven. Trading fees, spread or slippage can still affect the final result.

Under the tradeCompass discipline, that completes the bearish trade. No second short should be initiated using this same published map.

However, the bullish opportunity remains available if Bitcoin subsequently breaks above $80,860 and demonstrates sustained strength.

The lesson is simple: Take some profit, protect the remainder and let the market decide whether the larger move develops.

Educational only. Trade at your own risk.

---------- Previously published ------------

Bitcoin is approaching an important decision point for swing traders. Sellers have demonstrated their strength, but buyers are showing signs of defending the $80,000 area. The latest investingLive tradeCompass maps two conditional scenarios: bullish above $80,860 and bearish below $79,870.

The challenge is distinguishing a temporary rebound from a more durable recovery, or a brief dip from another significant breakdown.

Bitcoin tradeCompass: The bullish and bearish levels

The tradeCompass identifies two directional thresholds. Traders can use them to prepare for either outcome rather than commit to a prediction.

Bullish Bitcoin above $80,860

A sustained move above $80,860 would strengthen the case that Bitcoin's recent stabilization is developing into a more meaningful recovery.

The potential bullish profit targets are:

The first target at $81,770 represents the initial opportunity to secure a partial profit. The higher targets provide objectives if buying momentum develops into a more substantial swing.

Importantly, the bullish threshold has already been tested. On October 25, Binance BTC/USDC traded as high as approximately $80,942 before retreating below $80,860. A subsequent market snapshot around 20:04 UTC showed Bitcoin near $80,453.

That brief crossing is not sufficient by itself to establish a confirmed breakout or an executed trade. Traders considering the bullish scenario should reassess whether price can regain and hold above the threshold.

Bearish Bitcoin below $79,870

A sustained breakdown below $79,870 would suggest that the latest attempts to establish support have failed, potentially putting sellers back in control.

The bearish profit targets are:

The first two targets are relatively close to the bearish threshold. The third and fourth require more meaningful downside continuation.

A breakdown would become more convincing if Bitcoin struggled to recover above the breached level after initially falling through it.

Between $79,870 and $80,860, the tradeCompass remains neutral. This is a decision zone, not a requirement to trade. Neither a failed bullish attempt nor a minor decline inside the zone automatically activates the bearish scenario.

Bitcoin sellers have the bigger trend, but buyers are challenging them

The recent price action presents an interesting conflict between different trading timeframes.

On October 22, Bitcoin experienced renewed selling pressure that undermined an earlier recovery attempt. The accompanying CME Bitcoin futures analysis showed elevated trading participation and a close near the lower end of the session's range.

That matters because sellers were not merely pushing prices temporarily lower. They demonstrated an ability to sustain downward pressure during an important session.

However, the subsequent price action offers a reason not to become overly committed to the bearish outlook.

On October 24, Bitcoin briefly traded down toward $79,133 on Binance BTC/USDC before recovering. That rejection was accompanied by unusually high trading activity in the relevant hourly observation.

Additional shorter-term observations on October 25 showed repeated unsuccessful attempts to sustain lower prices and improving intraday lows around the $80,000 to $80,440 region.

These developments suggest that buyers are becoming more willing to defend the lower trading area.

There is an important distinction, however, between buyers defending support and buyers establishing a new bullish trend.

The daily structure still showed bearish characteristics in the October 25 analysis. The shorter-term recovery signals had not overturned that broader weakness.

For Bitcoin swing traders, this distinction matters. A convincing move above $80,860 could create an attractive tactical bullish opportunity without necessarily confirming that the broader correction has ended.

Likewise, another successful defense around $80,000 does not guarantee that support will hold on the next test.

The first profit target matters for more than taking profits

One of the most useful principles of the investingLive tradeCompass is that trade management deserves as much attention as the initial direction.

For either scenario, traders following the suggested plan can consider two actions after reaching TP1:

  1. Take a partial profit on the position.

  2. Move the protective stop on the remaining position to the actual entry price.

For a bullish trade, that consideration arises at $81,770. For a bearish trade, it arises at $79,630.

The purpose is to reduce the remaining exposure while allowing part of the position to participate if a larger move develops.

Moving a stop to entry does not guarantee a completely risk-free outcome. Trading costs, spread, slippage and execution conditions can still produce losses.

Traders should also establish an appropriate initial protective stop before entering a position. The tradeCompass's opposite activation threshold is not automatically the appropriate stop, and position size should reflect the risk of the actual setup.

Why swing traders should avoid repeatedly chasing the same signal

The tradeCompass has another principle intended to discourage overtrading.

Each published tradeCompass allows a maximum of one completed bullish trade and one completed bearish trade under its suggested discipline.

If a trader enters a long position and that trade eventually concludes, the bullish opportunity from this particular publication is considered used, regardless of whether the trade made money, lost money or reached only its first profit target.

The same rule applies independently to the bearish scenario.

An unfilled order does not count as a completed opportunity, and an open position with a remaining runner is still part of the original trade.

The opposite direction can remain available if its conditions subsequently develop, but reversing after a losing trade should not be automatic.

This approach encourages selectivity rather than repeatedly entering whenever Bitcoin fluctuates around a familiar price.

What could make Bitcoin's next swing more convincing?

The bullish and bearish scenarios have different confirmation requirements, but they share an important principle: crossing a level is not the same as sustaining a move beyond it.

For bulls, the next improvement would be a renewed move above $80,860 that can hold. Depending on the trader's existing strategy, confirmation might involve a candle closing above the threshold, a successful retest or another independently validated entry signal.

For bears, renewed acceptance below $79,870 would indicate that the recovery attempts around $80,000 are failing.

The extended targets in both directions should be understood as potential objectives rather than forecasts of imminent moves.

For now, the central Bitcoin question is whether buyers can turn their recent defensive activity into sustained upside progress.

Above $80,860, the bullish tradeCompass becomes relevant. Below $79,870, the bearish opportunity becomes relevant. Between those levels, patience may be the more useful position.

For a fuller explanation of how these conditional scenarios work, read the investingLive guide to using tradeCompass.

The Fed may leave interest rates unchanged this week. So why could Bitcoin still move?

Bitcoin traders have another important event to watch this week: the US Federal Reserve's interest rate decision on Wednesday, October 28.

The Federal Reserve, often called the Fed, influences how expensive it is to borrow money. Higher interest rates can make safer investments, such as government bonds, more attractive compared with riskier assets like Bitcoin and other cryptocurrencies.

But markets often react more to what the Fed says about future interest rates than to the actual decision.

What does the market expect?

According to an October 20 Reuters survey cited in the analysis, 94 out of 100 economists expect the Fed to leave rates unchanged at 3.75% to 4.00% this Wednesday.

The supplied survey also reports that all 100 economists anticipate another rate increase in December.

That means leaving rates unchanged in October would not be particularly surprising. What could move Bitcoin is whether the Fed sounds more or less concerned about inflation and the need for further rate increases.

Three possible scenarios for Bitcoin and crypto

Scenario 1: Expected outcome - The Fed holds rates and remains cautious

The Fed leaves interest rates unchanged and signals that another increase in December is still likely.

Because markets already expect this, the decision might not provide Bitcoin with a strong reason to rise or fall.

Possible crypto reaction: Bitcoin remains choppy and directionless, with buyers and sellers continuing to compete around $80,000. Altcoins may also struggle to establish a convincing recovery.

For our tradeCompass, Bitcoin remaining between $79,870 and $80,860 would favor patience rather than forcing a directional trade.

Scenario 2: Bullish surprise - The Fed signals fewer rate increases

The Fed leaves rates unchanged but unexpectedly suggests that inflation is becoming less concerning, making another rate increase in December less certain.

This would be meaningful because investors expecting higher interest rates might suddenly reconsider their outlook.

Possible crypto reaction: Bitcoin rallies as investors become more willing to take risks. Ethereum and other cryptocurrencies could also benefit, particularly if the US dollar and bond yields decline.

For our tradeCompass, a sustained break above $80,860 would bring the bullish targets into focus, starting at $81,770, followed by $85,200.

Scenario 3: Bearish surprise - The Fed raises rates or warns of more hikes

The Fed unexpectedly increases interest rates immediately, or leaves them unchanged but suggests that inflation is serious enough to require several additional increases.

This would be a more aggressive message than markets currently expect.

Possible crypto reaction: Bitcoin and other cryptocurrencies could sell off sharply as investors reduce exposure to riskier assets. A stronger US dollar and rising bond yields could add pressure.

For our tradeCompass, a sustained move below $79,870 would activate the bearish scenario, with initial targets at $79,630 and $79,310. If selling continues, the lower targets become relevant.

What should Bitcoin traders watch?

The Fed decision is scheduled for 2:00 p.m. New York time on Wednesday, followed by the press conference at 2:30 p.m.

Traders can also watch the US dollar and Treasury yields for clues about how financial markets interpret the announcement.

And there is another potential catalyst on Thursday, October 29, when important US inflation (PCE) and economic growth (GDP) figures are scheduled for release.

The important lesson: Markets respond to surprises, not simply whether news sounds good or bad. Even a decision to do nothing can move Bitcoin if the Fed's message changes what investors expect next.

That is another reason to use the tradeCompass as a conditional trading map, rather than trying to predict the Fed's decision or Bitcoin's immediate reaction.

Educational only. Trade at your own risk. Cryptocurrency markets can be highly volatile, and losses may exceed expectations when trading with leverage.

This article was written by Itai Levitan at investinglive.com.

item.title: Weekend - China warns of countermeasures as US Treasury widens tech investment curbs to biotech
item.description:
The proposal adds to already tense US-China relations and keeps headline risk elevated for Chinese technology and biotech stocks, including US-listed ADRs and the Hang Seng Tech index. Biotech is the sector most directly exposed, since it is the newly targeted industry and has relied more heavily on cross-border funding than areas already under restriction. Beijing has not named the countermeasures it might take, and that vagueness tends to keep investors cautious until the response becomes clear. A long public comment period leaves time for negotiation, but it also stretches the uncertainty out for months, which could weigh on risk appetite toward China-exposed assets and the offshore yuan if rhetoric escalates.

--

Washington wants to stop US capital from funding China’s next generation of strategic technology, and Beijing is signalling that it will not take the move quietly.

Summary:

  • On Thursday the US Treasury proposed a rule expanding the Outbound Investment Security Program, tightening limits on US investment in hypersonics, quantum, high-performance computing, supercomputing and AI in China, Russia and North Korea
  • The rule also adds biotechnology to the targeted sectors, an addition sought by Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent
  • China’s commerce ministry said on Saturday the move discriminatorily widens China-related restrictions, overstretches national security and would damage bilateral economic ties
  • Beijing said it will monitor developments and reserves the right to take unspecified countermeasures
  • The proposal faces a public comment period before a final rule is issued
  • Separately, the State Department this week sanctioned five Chinese companies linked to former Google engineer Linwei Ding, convicted this year of stealing AI trade secrets, drawing further objections from Beijing

China has urged the United States to reconsider a proposed rule that would further restrict American investment in its technology sector, warning that the measure would harm trade relations and that Beijing reserves the right to retaliate.

China’s commerce ministry voiced firm opposition on Saturday in a statement carried by the state-run Global Times, according to a report by The Hill. A ministry spokesperson said the proposal widens China-related investment restrictions in a discriminatory way and described it as a classic example of stretching the concept of national security too far. The ministry said it would watch subsequent developments closely, warned the rule would damage economic ties between the two countries, and said China retains the right to take corresponding measures, without specifying what those might be.

The US Treasury Department unveiled the proposal on Thursday. It would expand existing restrictions under the Outbound Investment Security Program covering hypersonic systems, quantum information technologies, high-performance computing, supercomputing and artificial intelligence. The program aims to stop a small group of countries designated as foreign adversaries, namely China, Russia and North Korea, from using US capital to advance their own technological capabilities.

The proposed rule would also bring the biotechnology industry within the program’s scope, an addition that Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent had pushed for, according to a department press release. Bessent said the changes would strengthen the program and prevent adversaries from using American investment to build critical technologies that threaten US national security.

The measure must go through a public comment period before Treasury issues a final version, leaving room for revisions and for further diplomatic exchanges in the meantime.

The proposal lands days after the State Department imposed sanctions on five Chinese companies connected to Linwei Ding, a former Google engineer convicted earlier this year of stealing trade secrets related to artificial intelligence. Beijing also objected to those penalties, saying they seriously harm the legitimate rights and interests of Chinese businesses. Taken together, the two moves underline Washington’s widening focus on technology and capital flows as a front in its rivalry with China. Beijing’s eventual response is now the key variable for investors and policymakers alike.

This article was written by Eamonn Sheridan at investinglive.com.

item.title: Goldman Sachs cuts Kospi target 25% to 9,000, still sees over 60% upside
item.description:
The cut removes one of the most bullish institutional Kospi targets from the table, but the bank’s insistence on deep value gives contrarian investors a framework for buying into weakness rather than chasing the selloff lower. Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix remain the swing factor, since any stabilisation in sentiment toward AI capital spending would likely feed directly into the index given their weight. The sector preferences point to a possible rotation inside Korean equities, away from memory chips and toward power, industrials and domestically focused names, which could limit the downside for the broader market even if chip stocks stay under pressure. Foreign investor flows will be the key signal of whether the valuation argument is gaining traction.

--- Goldman Sachs has blinked on its Kospi call but not folded, arguing that a market trading at about four times earnings is pricing in a chip downturn far worse than is likely.

Summary:

  • Goldman Sachs lowered its 12-month Kospi target to 9,000 from 12,000, a 25% cut, citing AI investment concerns and more conservative valuations
  • The index has fallen more than 35% from its June peak, and the new target still implies upside of more than 60%
  • The Kospi’s 12-month forward P/E has dropped to around four, a level not seen across 18 major markets since 2006, and roughly half the valuation of Indonesian stocks
  • Goldman estimates current chip valuations imply a 65% fall in sector earnings in 2027, which it considers overly pessimistic
  • Stocks outside memory chips, about half the index, trade at under eight times forward earnings
  • Preferred themes include power, industrials, corporate governance plays, domestic recovery and Korean popular culture

Goldman Sachs has cut its 12-month target for South Korea’s Kospi Index by a quarter, lowering it to 9,000 from 12,000, as worries over artificial intelligence spending and a shift toward more conservative equity valuations weigh on the market. Even so, the bank argues that Korean shares now look deeply undervalued, and its new target still implies a gain of more than 60% from current levels.

The downgrade follows a slide of more than 35% in the benchmark from its June peak. Goldman had raised its Kospi target in June and kept its bullish stance even as global technology stocks began to retreat on concerns about the scale of AI investment.

South Korea’s market has been especially exposed to that shift because of its heavy concentration in memory chipmakers Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix. Both have been major beneficiaries of demand for chips used in AI infrastructure, which has turned the Kospi into a widely watched gauge of investor sentiment toward the technology. As concerns have grown about rising financing costs, enormous infrastructure outlays and uncertain returns on that spending, selling has spread across Korean equities.

Goldman’s strategists said the market is now discounting an excessively bleak outlook for corporate fundamentals. The Kospi’s 12-month forward price-to-earnings ratio has fallen to around four, a level not seen across 18 major markets since 2006, and Korean stocks now trade at roughly half the valuation of Indonesian equities. By the bank’s estimates, current semiconductor valuations imply a 65% collapse in sector earnings in 2027, a scenario the strategists regard as overly pessimistic.

The valuation argument extends beyond chips. Companies outside the memory sector, which make up about half the index, trade at under eight times forward earnings, according to the bank.

Despite trimming its headline target, Goldman continues to favour selected areas of the market, including power, industrials, stocks tied to corporate governance reform, and companies set to benefit from a domestic economic recovery and the global reach of Korean popular culture. Whether investors embrace that value case is likely to depend on how sentiment toward AI spending evolves in the months ahead. 

This article was written by Eamonn Sheridan at investinglive.com.

item.title: RBA’s Hunter says inflation job not done after four hikes, November rise in view
item.description:
The comments should keep the Australian dollar supported, at the margin, on rate differentials and hold short-dated Australian government bond yields elevated, with markets likely to lean further toward a November hike unless Wednesday’s inflation data surprise lower. Oil is the swing variable: renewed escalation in the US-Iran war that lifts crude would deepen the RBA’s concern about second-round effects and raise the risk of tightening beyond November. A sustained easing in crude, by contrast, would give the board more room to signal a pause after its next move. Property-linked stocks and consumer discretionary names on the ASX remain exposed to a higher-for-longer policy path.

-

Earlier:

Four hikes in, the RBA’s forecasting chief says the job is not finished, with war-driven oil costs working their way into supply chains and a fifth increase looking likely on November 3.

Summary:

  • RBA Assistant Governor Sarah Hunter said the bank has “not quite yet” done enough to bring inflation under control, in a television interview aired Sunday evening Australian time
  • She declined to pre-empt the board’s decision but said policymakers remain committed to getting inflation down; the next meeting is November 3
  • Hunter said higher oil prices linked to the US-Iran war are becoming embedded in some supply chains, with more of that effect expected
  • Deputy Governor Andrew Hauser said on Wednesday the inflation outlook is materially worse than the bank assessed in August
  • The cash rate stands at 4.6%, a 15-year high, after four hikes this year; Hunter said falling house prices are not causing systemic financial stress
  • Third-quarter CPI is due Wednesday, with trimmed mean inflation expected at 3.6%, similar to the prior quarter

Reserve Bank of Australia Assistant Governor Sarah Hunter said the central bank has not yet finished its fight against inflation, reinforcing expectations that policymakers will raise interest rates again when they meet on November 3.

Speaking in an interview with Nine Network’s 60 Minutes, broadcast on Sunday evening Australian time, Hunter noted that the board had delivered four rate increases this year to tackle persistent price pressures. Asked whether that tightening had been enough to tame inflation, she replied “not quite yet.” She declined to front-run the board’s next decision, but stressed that policymakers remained committed to bringing inflation down.

Her remarks build on comments from Deputy Governor Andrew Hauser on Wednesday, when he said the inflation outlook had become materially worse since the bank’s August assessment. Those remarks had already lifted market expectations for a hike at the November meeting.

Hunter, who oversees economic forecasting at the RBA, pointed to the ongoing US-Iran war as a source of renewed pressure. Higher oil prices linked to the conflict are beginning to become embedded in some supply chains, she said, adding that the bank expects more of that pass-through to come. The comment suggests the RBA is increasingly concerned that the energy shock is spreading beyond fuel prices into the broader cost base of the economy, which would make inflation more persistent and harder to bring back down.

The RBA lifted its cash rate in late September to 4.6%, the highest level in 15 years. A further increase would add downward pressure on Australian property prices, which have already been falling. Hunter said the decline in house prices was not, so far, creating systemic financial stress across the system, a signal that the bank does not see housing weakness as a reason to hold off.

Attention now turns to Wednesday, when Australia’s third-quarter consumer price data are released. The trimmed mean measure of underlying inflation is expected at 3.6%, broadly in line with the previous quarter. Governor Michele Bullock and other policymakers are also scheduled to appear before parliament the same day, giving them another opportunity to set out their thinking ahead of the decision. A reading in line with forecasts, combined with the oil-driven pressure Hunter described, would likely leave a November hike as the market’s base case.
